title: House Construction Acceptance in Vietnam 2026: Steps and Records
desc: House acceptance under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 207/2026/ND-CP: work, stage and completion acceptance; who signs and which documents to keep.
summary: The acceptance steps when building a house: work, stage and completion acceptance; the content of records, signatories and documents homeowners should keep under the Construction Law 2025.
body: p

Acceptance is the step where the homeowner checks and confirms whether the work the contractor has done matches the design and the quality required. From 1 July 2026, acceptance follows Article 57 of the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 207/2026/ND-CP.
h2
1. What types of acceptance are there?
p
Under Clause 1, Article 57 of the Construction Law 2025, acceptance includes:
ul
Work acceptance during construction (reinforcement, formwork, foundation concrete, columns, floor slabs, etc.); stage acceptance for moving on to the next construction step when necessary.
Completion acceptance of a work item or the whole work before it is put into use.
p

A work may be put into use only after it has been accepted as meeting the design requirements, regulations and standards (Clause 2, Article 57). The investor - for a private house, the homeowner - is responsible for organizing acceptance; those who sign acceptance are responsible for the work they confirm.
h2
2. Acceptance of individual work on site
p
Under Article 22 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP:
ul

The construction supervisor and the contractor's technical person in charge carry out acceptance on site, based on construction drawings, technical instructions, regulations and material test results.
The supervisor must carry out acceptance within 24 hours of the contractor's request; if not agreeing, the supervisor must state the reason in writing.
The record states: the name of the work, time, place, the signatories, the conclusion on whether it is accepted, and repair requirements (if any).
p

For a private house, the homeowner organizes construction supervision personally and is encouraged to prepare and keep records under the Decree; houses of 7 floors or more or with 2 or more basements must organize construction and supervision under the Decree (Clause 3, Article 10). So even if not mandatory, the homeowner should sign acceptance records for important parts such as the foundation, columns and floor beams before concrete is poured.
h2
3. Stage acceptance
p

The homeowner and the contractor agree on their own to hold acceptance when a stage or a part of the work ends (for example, the foundation is done or the rough structure is done), or when a work package ends. The timing, content and participants are agreed by the two parties; the result is recorded in a written record (Article 23 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).
h2
4. Completion acceptance of the work
p
Under Article 24 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, the investor organizes completion acceptance when:
ol
All work has been fully built according to the approved design documents;
All work, parts and stages during construction have been fully accepted;
Test, inspection and trial-run results meet the design requirements;
Fire prevention and fighting and environmental protection rules in construction have been complied with.
p

The completion acceptance record must state the conclusion on whether it is accepted, repair requirements, and especially the start of the warranty and the warranty period. If there are minor outstanding items that do not affect load-bearing capacity or function, conditional acceptance is possible, stating the outstanding items and the deadline to remedy them (Clause 3, Article 24).
h2
5. Handover and the documents homeowners should keep
p

Before handover, the contractor must give the investor the as-built drawings, operating procedures (if any), maintenance procedures, and the list of equipment and spare parts (Clause 3, Article 58 of the Construction Law 2025; Article 30 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP). The investor prepares and keeps the work completion file (Article 28). The homeowner should keep at least:
ul
The construction contract, design drawings, and building permit (if any);
The acceptance records and material test results (concrete, steel, etc.);
The as-built drawings, maintenance instructions and equipment warranty cards.
p
This set of documents is needed when registering the house on the land certificate - see As-built completion and registering the house on the land certificate 2026.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal documents. Large-scale works with a major impact on public safety must also have their acceptance checked by a state authority (Article 25 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP). Agree the acceptance schedule clearly in the construction contract.
